# `redundant-bool-comparison`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: idiomatic · Default: off · Fixes: fix all · Options: none

Reports a proven boolean compared with `true` or `false`.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Using the boolean or its negation directly is shorter and makes the condition's
intent easier to scan.

## When it fires

It applies only when the operand is known to be `bool`, avoiding rewrites of
user-defined comparison semantics.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
fn check(ready: bool) void {
    if (ready == true) {}
}
```
